status: Owner-local Inventory reservation-source fences are closed and the stock-register/receipt SSR cutover is register-sufficient when the native source is configured. inventory/feature-stock-register and inventory/feature-receipts remain partial because no authenticated browser cohort was run and the retained Commerce fulfillment writer still does not call the Inventory receipt seam in the same transaction.
workspaceNote: The shared worktree also contained other owners' uncommitted work. Those files were preserved and not edited by this slice.

scope.stockRegister: The current Company/branch register still reads Inventory-owned relations in the caller's serializable unit. Its source fence now includes Field Service and Manufacturing reservations in addition to POS and Sales because inventory_active_reservations unions all four sources. The register is PostgreSQL-tested to include those reservations in reserved quantity.
scope.receipts: The receipt source derives reserved quantity from the same inventory_active_reservations view and now fences POS, Sales, Field Service and Manufacturing reservation tables before its first read. The existing purchase, warehouse, branch, lot/serial, quarantine, over-receipt, replay and rollback guards are unchanged.
scope.ssr: The stock view chooses the configured native register first, then native availability, and falls back to retained Commerce rows only when neither native source is configured. A configured empty register stays empty instead of leaking legacy rows. The supply stock page and the Commerce stock view now render from the native register when Commerce posting setup raises COMMERCE_SETUP_REQUIRED, so the register no longer depends on availability configuration or Commerce posting setup.
notClaimed: No authenticated desktop or mobile browser journey was run.
No native Commerce purchase-fulfillment command was implemented; the retained FulfillmentForm/fulfillOrder write path is unchanged.
No production StockReceiptQualityPort implementation exists; the PostgreSQL test port is unchanged.
No stock-register cursor pagination or default-on rollout was added; rows remain bounded.
The full tests/config TypeScript project was not green because unrelated uncommitted learning and PMS test files had type errors. The Inventory transport test itself typechecks standalone.

behavior.registerFence: lock_stock_register_sources holds SHARE locks on pos_reservations, inventory_order_reservations, field_service_part_reservations and manufacturing_material_reservations before reading the register.
behavior.receiptFence: lock_stock_receipt_sources holds SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE locks on the same four reservation sources plus the retained Commerce/Inventory receipt relations before reading or applying a receipt.
behavior.reservedArithmetic: A register row reserves the sum of POS, Sales, Field Service and Manufacturing quantities. A receipt source reports the same reserved quantity for the selected warehouse/product.
behavior.fenceNegative: A concurrent UPDATE against each reservation source waits and fails with SQLSTATE 55P03 under a 150 ms lock timeout while the Inventory read unit holds its fence; an unrelated support_tickets update succeeds under the same timeout.
behavior.ssrSelection: register > availability > retained Commerce rows. A configured empty register returns zero rows and its own currency; it never falls back to legacy rows.
behavior.ssrFallback: The Commerce stock view builds an empty Commerce shell only for COMMERCE_SETUP_REQUIRED when the native register is configured. Any other configured failure still follows the existing page-error path.
